title: A Market Scan Starts With What You Exclude
topic: Why a reliable research universe starts with instrument identity, tradability, quote quality, completed data and honest market scope before any candidate ranking

scenes.title: A SCAN IS NOT A STOCK LIST
scenes.overlay: Define the universe before the signal.
scenes.narration: A market scan is not just a list of tickers. It is a definition of what the research can actually trust.

scenes.title: START WITH THE INSTRUMENT
scenes.overlay: Active does not always mean tradable.
scenes.narration: Start with the asset catalogue. Confirm the instrument class, listing venue, current status and whether it is tradable through the route you intend to use. Data availability and execution availability are not always the same thing.

scenes.title: INSTRUMENT TYPES DIFFER
scenes.overlay: A wrapper is not the same as a share.
scenes.narration: Then separate instruments that answer different questions. A common share is not an exchange-traded fund, a warrant or a preferred security. A wrapper can carry a different structure and risk. The SEC notes that leveraged and inverse ETFs are designed around daily objectives, so longer-period results can diverge from the underlying benchmark.

scenes.title: CHECK THE QUOTE QUALITY
scenes.overlay: Spread and depth are part of the evidence.
scenes.narration: Next, test whether the quote is usable. A wide bid-ask spread, thin activity or inconsistent volume can make a screen price look more precise than the market really is. Liquidity is part of data quality, not decoration.

scenes.title: USE COMPLETED, TIMESTAMPED BARS
scenes.overlay: A moving candle is not a final observation.
scenes.narration: Check the history too. Missing sessions, abrupt symbol changes or too few completed observations can distort averages and momentum measures. Keep the timestamp with every bar, and make sure the interval has actually closed before using its final value.

scenes.title: DEFINE THE REAL MARKET SCOPE
scenes.overlay: Do not imply coverage you do not have.
scenes.narration: Now define the boundaries: which exchanges, which instrument types, what data feeds and what regions are genuinely connected. If a market is not connected, label it that way. Do not let a broad-looking watchlist imply coverage you do not have.

scenes.title: A UNIVERSE IS NOT A FORECAST
scenes.overlay: Scope first. Evidence second. Decisions last.
scenes.narration: Only after those checks should a candidate enter a research ranking. A clean universe does not predict a return and does not create a recommendation. It simply makes the next question more honest: is the evidence complete enough to continue? Paper-trading education only; not live-money performance; not investment advice; no guaranteed returns.

instagram_caption:
A market scan is only as reliable as the universe behind it. Start by checking what each instrument is, whether it is tradable through the intended route, whether its quote and history are usable, and which markets are genuinely connected. Different products can behave differently: the SEC notes that leveraged and inverse ETFs are built around daily objectives, so longer-period results can diverge from the underlying benchmark.

A clean research universe does not predict returns or create a recommendation. It makes the evidence easier to interpret.

claims.claim: Alpaca describes its assets endpoint as a master list for trade and data consumption, and notes that some listed assets are not tradable.
Alpaca historical stock bars are interval aggregates with timestamps and are returned in timestamp order.
The SEC notes leveraged and inverse ETFs are designed around daily objectives and longer-period performance may differ significantly from the underlying benchmark.
